topic: BOI filing — certifying officer personal liability under the CTA
body:
Most BOI discussions focus on whether you've filed.

The more important question is who certified it — and what they personally attested to.

FinCEN's BOI rule (31 CFR 1010.380) doesn't just require a report. It requires a certification by a beneficial owner or senior officer. That certification is a federal representation of fact.

When it's wrong, the penalties don't fall on the LLC in the abstract. They fall on the individual who signed.

**The exposure:**
— Civil: up to $591/day per violation (inflation-adjusted)
— Criminal: up to 2 years + $10,000 fine
— Standard: willful violation OR reckless disregard — not just intentional fraud

**The part most LLCs miss:**

BOI is a continuing obligation. If a beneficial owner changes their address, gets a new driver's license, or there's any change in who qualifies as a beneficial owner — you have 30 calendar days to file an update.

The certifying officer is responsible for the current report. Not the one filed two years ago.

If you have no process for collecting that information, you have no way to know when the 30-day clock starts running.

**The DAO problem:**

DAOs organized as Wyoming or Marshall Islands LLCs have a specific wrinkle: token-weighted governance means someone who can unilaterally pass governance proposals affecting the organization's direction may qualify as a beneficial owner under the 'substantial control' prong — regardless of whether they hold a formal title.

'Substantial control' isn't just equity. It includes authority over significant decisions. For some DAO governance structures, identifying who qualifies is a legal analysis, not a software question.

**The injunction cycle hangover:**

The December 2024–early 2025 injunctions created a compliance gap. Many domestic LLCs that should have filed by January 1, 2025 didn't. FinCEN hasn't issued blanket amnesty for that period.

If you're in that gap, the question isn't just whether to file now. It's whether your delay rises to the level of willful non-compliance, and whether voluntary disclosure is appropriate. That requires legal judgment.

Full analysis at the link in bio.
